questions.q: Per this lesson's recap, what is the correct order of the hard ceiling and default visibility, from broadest restriction to more specific?
options: License sets the hard ceiling, then the Role Hierarchy determines default record visibility on top of that
The Role Hierarchy is applied first, and licenses are irrelevant to access
Field-Level Security is applied before any other layer
Sharing Rules are applied before licenses are even assigned
questions.explain: The lesson recaps license as the hard ceiling first, with the Role Hierarchy's default visibility building on top of it.

questions.q: According to this lesson, why can't SOQL syntax alone tell you whether a query's result is trustworthy?
options: SOQL can't tell you what a field actually means in this org, whether visibility rules are hiding records, or whether FLS is silently hiding a field -- only platform/data-model/security understanding can
SOQL queries are always technically incapable of returning wrong results
SOQL has nothing to do with Opportunity or Account objects
This course teaches that SOQL alone is always sufficient without any platform knowledge
questions.explain: The lesson's core point: a technically correct query on a wrong mental model produces a confidently wrong number.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the relationship between Profiles and Permission Sets, as recapped from Chapter 6?
options: A Profile is the mandatory, single baseline; Permission Sets are additive, stackable grants layered on top
Profiles and Permission Sets are functionally identical and interchangeable
Permission Sets replace Profiles entirely in every modern Salesforce org
A user can have multiple Profiles but at most one Permission Set
questions.explain: This matches the Lesson 28 distinction recapped here: one mandatory Profile, any number of additive Permission Sets.
